## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Anantarāpayuttakathā* (Kv 13.3) is the third discourse of the thirteenth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, located in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The debate concerns the status of an individual bound to an immediate destiny (*anantarāpayutta puggala*)—specifically someone guilty of one of the grave offenses entailing immediate retribution (*anantaravipāka*), such as matricide, parricide, murdering an arahant, shedding the blood of a Buddha, or causing a schism in the Saṅgha—and investigates whether such a person is capable or incapable of entering the assurance of correctness (*sammattaniyāma*) [Bareau 1955]. In his study of early Buddhist schools, André Bareau notes sectarian positions regarding whether this individual can enter the path of right determination or is definitively precluded from it [Bareau 1955].

SuttaCentral records one modern language translation of the text and provides no curated parallels [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus shows that Kv 13.3 shares formulaic segments internally within the Pali canon, notably with other *Kathāvatthu* chapters such as the *Sattakkhattuparamakathā* (Kv 12.5) and the *Dhammataṇhānadukkhasamudayotikathā* (Kv 13.10), alongside recurring doctrinal phrases matched in the *Chakkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 6), the *Kusalattika* of the *Paṭṭhāna* (Patthana 1.2), and the *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also identifies low-scoring computational alignments with Tibetan Mahāyāna texts, including the *Daśacakrakṣitigarbhasūtra* (D0239), though these constitute automatic machine matches rather than historical parallels [DharmaNexus].
